subproblem.title: Continuity from above: a density quotient dominated by σ(B_r(z)) has liminf at most σ({z})
subproblem.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ. Let σ be a Borel measure on ℝ^P with σ(K) < ∞ for every compact K ⊆ ℝ^P, let z ∈ ℝ^P, and let f : ℝ → [0, ∞] satisfy f(r) ≤ ω_n·ofReal(rⁿ)·σ(B_r(z)) for every r > 0, where ω_n = unitBallVolume n and B_r(z) is the open ball. Then liminf_{r→0+} f(r)/(ω_n·ofReal(rⁿ)) ≤ σ({z}). The liminf is taken along the filter 𝓝[>] 0 on ℝ, and the quotient is division in [0, ∞].
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (σ : Measure (Euclid P)) (z : Euclid P) (f : ℝ → ℝ≥0∞), (∀ K : Set (Euclid P), IsCompact K → σ K < ∞) → (∀ r : ℝ, 0 < r → f r ≤ unitBallVolume n * ENNReal.ofReal (r ^ n) * σ (ball z r)) → liminf (fun r : ℝ => f r / (unitBallVolume n * ENNReal.ofReal (r ^ n))) (𝓝[>] 0) ≤ σ {z}
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: step 2 ("Density bound") of the parent proof. It is stated for an arbitrary function f in place of r ↦ ν(B_r(x)) and an arbitrary point z in place of q x = x − p_V x; in the parent, the domination f(r) ≤ ω_nrⁿσ(B_r(q x)) is step 1.
Notation: a(r) := ω_n·ofReal(rⁿ) ∈ [0, ∞]. All arithmetic is in [0, ∞]. B_r(z) is the open ball and B̄_r(z) the closed ball.
1. (Pointwise quotient bound.) Let r > 0. By hypothesis f(r) ≤ a(r)·σ(B_r(z)) = σ(B_r(z))·a(r). In [0, ∞], u ≤ v·w implies u/w ≤ v for all u, v, w (Mathlib ENNReal.div_le_of_le_mul). No side condition on w is needed: if w = 0 then u ≤ v·0 = 0, so u/w = 0·∞ = 0 ≤ v; if w = ∞ then u/w = u·0 = 0 ≤ v; otherwise divide. Hence f(r)/a(r) ≤ σ(B_r(z)) for every r > 0. The set (0, ∞) belongs to the filter 𝓝[>] 0 (self_mem_nhdsWithin), so this inequality holds eventually along 𝓝[>] 0.
2. (Shrinking balls.) For 0 < i ≤ j, B_i(z) ⊆ B_j(z) (ball_subset_ball), and every B_r(z) is open, hence Borel. The intersection ⋂_{r>0}B_r(z) equals {z}: z ∈ B_r(z) for every r > 0 because dist(z, z) = 0 < r; and if y ≠ z then r := dist(y, z) > 0 while y ∉ B_r(z). Finally σ(B_1(z)) ≤ σ(B̄_1(z)) < ∞, because B_1(z) ⊆ B̄_1(z), the closed ball B̄_1(z) is compact in the proper space ℝ^P (isCompact_closedBall), and σ is finite on compact sets.
3. (Continuity from above.) By step 2, the family s(r) := B_r(z), r > 0, consists of measurable sets, is monotone in r on (0, ∞), and has a member of finite measure (r = 1). Continuity of measures from above along r ↓ 0 (Mathlib tendsto_measure_biInter_gt with a = 0) therefore gives σ(B_r(z)) → σ(⋂_{r>0}B_r(z)) = σ({z}) as r → 0 along 𝓝[>] 0.
4. (Liminf.) By step 1 and monotonicity of liminf under an eventual inequality (Filter.liminf_le_liminf), liminf_{r→0+}f(r)/a(r) ≤ liminf_{r→0+}σ(B_r(z)); in the complete lattice [0, ∞] the boundedness side conditions of that lemma hold automatically. The filter 𝓝[>] 0 on ℝ is nontrivial, so by step 3 the right-hand liminf equals the limit σ({z}) (Filter.Tendsto.liminf_eq). Hence liminf_{r→0+}f(r)/(ω_n·ofReal(rⁿ)) ≤ σ({z}). ∎
proof_key_steps: For r > 0, f(r) ≤ σ(B_r(z))·a(r) gives f(r)/a(r) ≤ σ(B_r(z)) in [0, ∞] (ENNReal.div_le_of_le_mul, no side condition), eventually along 𝓝[>] 0.
The balls B_r(z) are Borel, increase with r, have intersection {z} over r > 0, and σ(B_1(z)) ≤ σ(B̄_1(z)) < ∞.
Continuity from above (tendsto_measure_biInter_gt) gives σ(B_r(z)) → σ({z}) along 𝓝[>] 0.
Monotonicity of liminf and Tendsto.liminf_eq give liminf f(r)/a(r) ≤ σ({z}).

audit.reason: The generic function contract matches the prose. ENNReal.div_le_of_le_mul justifies division without additional denominator conditions. Compact-ball finiteness supplies continuity from above, the shrinking intersection is exactly {z}, and liminf monotonicity yields the conclusion. Measurability of f is unnecessary.

subproblem.title: A product measure whose transversal measure is carried by a countable set is a countable sum of weighted parallel planes
subproblem.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, V ⊆ ℝ^P a linear subspace, σ a Borel measure on ℝ^P, and Z ⊆ ℝ^P a countable set with σ(ℝ^P∖Z) = 0. Let ν be a Borel measure on ℝ^P with ν(A) = ∫⁻_{t∈V}σ({y : t + y ∈ A}) dHⁿ(t) for every Borel A ⊆ ℝ^P (Hⁿ = μHE[n]). Then ν = Σ_{w∈Z}σ({w})·Hⁿ⌞{y : y − w ∈ V}. That is, ν is the Measure.sum, over the subtype Z, of the measures σ({w})•(Hⁿ restricted to {y : y − w ∈ V}).
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (ν σ : Measure (Euclid P)) (V : Submodule ℝ (Euclid P)) (Z : Set (Euclid P)), Z.Countable → σ Zᶜ = 0 → (∀ A : Set (Euclid P), MeasurableSet A → ν A = ∫⁻ t in (V : Set (Euclid P)), σ ((fun y => t + y) ⁻¹' A) ∂μHE[n]) → ν = Measure.sum (fun w : Z => σ {(w : Euclid P)} • (μHE[n]).restrict {y : Euclid P | y - w ∈ V})
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: steps 5 ("σ is a sum of point masses") and 6 ("ν is a sum of planes") of the parent proof. In the parent, Z = {w ∈ V^⊥ : ofReal c ≤ σ({w})} is countable with σ(ℝ^P∖Z) = 0 by steps 3–4. Neither the dimension of V nor Z ⊆ V^⊥ is used here.
Notation: (D) is the hypothesis ν(A) = ∫⁻_{t∈V}σ({y : t + y ∈ A}) dHⁿ(t) for Borel A. Sums Σ_{w∈Z} are unconditional sums (tsum) in [0, ∞] over the subtype Z, which is a countable type because Z is a countable set (Set.Countable.to_subtype). 1_S is the indicator function of S, with values in {0, 1} ⊆ [0, ∞].
1. (σ is a sum of point masses.) Let S ⊆ ℝ^P be Borel. Since σ(ℝ^P∖Z) = 0, σ(S) = σ(S ∩ Z) (measure_inter_conull). Moreover S ∩ Z = ⋃_{w∈Z}(S ∩ {w}): a point y ∈ S ∩ Z lies in the term with w = y, and every term is contained in S ∩ Z. The sets S ∩ {w} (w ∈ Z) are Borel, since singletons are closed. They are pairwise disjoint, since for w ≠ w′ the singletons {w} and {w′} are disjoint. The index type Z is countable, so countable additivity (measure_iUnion) gives σ(S ∩ Z) = Σ_{w∈Z}σ(S ∩ {w}). For each w ∈ Z: if w ∈ S then S ∩ {w} = {w}, so σ(S ∩ {w}) = σ({w}) = σ({w})·1_S(w); if w ∉ S then S ∩ {w} = ∅, so σ(S ∩ {w}) = 0 = σ({w})·1_S(w). Hence σ(S) = Σ_{w∈Z}σ({w})·1_S(w) for every Borel S.
2. (Insertion into (D).) Let A ⊆ ℝ^P be Borel and t ∈ ℝ^P. The set S_t := {y : t + y ∈ A} is Borel, being the preimage of A under the continuous map y ↦ t + y, and 1_{S_t}(w) = 1_A(t + w) for every w. By step 1, σ(S_t) = Σ_{w∈Z}σ({w})·1_A(t + w). Therefore (D) gives ν(A) = ∫⁻_{t∈V}Σ_{w∈Z}σ({w})·1_A(t + w) dHⁿ(t).
3. (Exchange of sum and integral.) For each w ∈ Z, the function t ↦ 1_A(t + w) is Borel measurable (A is Borel and t ↦ t + w is continuous), hence so is t ↦ σ({w})·1_A(t + w). Since the index type Z is countable, the monotone convergence theorem for series of nonnegative measurable functions (lintegral_tsum) and pulling out the constant (lintegral_const_mul) give ν(A) = Σ_{w∈Z}σ({w})·∫⁻_{t∈V}1_A(t + w) dHⁿ(t).
4. (Translation.) Fix w ∈ Z and put A − w := {t : t + w ∈ A}, a Borel set with 1_A(t + w) = 1_{A−w}(t). Then ∫⁻_{t∈V}1_{A−w}(t) dHⁿ(t) = (Hⁿ⌞V)(A − w) = Hⁿ((A − w) ∩ V) (lintegral_indicator_one, Measure.restrict_apply). The translation τ(t) := t + w is an isometry of ℝ^P (isometry_add_right). Hⁿ = μHE[n] is invariant under isometries: Hⁿ(τ(S)) = Hⁿ(S) for every S ⊆ ℝ^P (Isometry.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_image). Moreover τ((A − w) ∩ V) = A ∩ {y : y − w ∈ V}. Indeed, if t + w ∈ A and t ∈ V, then y := τ(t) = t + w ∈ A and y − w = t ∈ V. Conversely, if y ∈ A and y − w ∈ V, then t := y − w satisfies t + w = y ∈ A, t ∈ V and τ(t) = y. Hence ∫⁻_{t∈V}1_A(t + w) dHⁿ(t) = Hⁿ(A ∩ {y : y − w ∈ V}) = (Hⁿ⌞{y : y − w ∈ V})(A) (Measure.restrict_apply; A is Borel).
5. (Conclusion.) By steps 3 and 4, ν(A) = Σ_{w∈Z}σ({w})·(Hⁿ⌞{y : y − w ∈ V})(A). This equals Σ_{w∈Z}(σ({w})•Hⁿ⌞{y : y − w ∈ V})(A) (Measure.smul_apply), which equals (Measure.sum_{w∈Z}σ({w})•Hⁿ⌞{y : y − w ∈ V})(A) because A is Borel (Measure.sum_apply). This holds for every Borel A, so the two measures are equal (Measure.ext). ∎
proof_key_steps: For Borel S, σ(S) = σ(S ∩ Z) = Σ_{w∈Z}σ(S ∩ {w}) = Σ_{w∈Z}σ({w})·1_S(w), by countable additivity over the countable set Z.
Inserting this with S = {y : t + y ∈ A} into the product formula and exchanging sum and integral (lintegral_tsum) gives ν(A) = Σ_{w∈Z}σ({w})·Hⁿ(V ∩ {t : t + w ∈ A}).
Translation by w is an isometry carrying V ∩ {t : t + w ∈ A} onto A ∩ {y : y − w ∈ V}, and Hⁿ is isometry invariant, so ν(A) = Σ_{w∈Z}σ({w})·(Hⁿ⌞{y : y − w ∈ V})(A).
Measure.sum_apply and Measure.ext give the identity of measures.

audit.reason: Countable additivity over disjoint singletons establishes the atomic expansion. The measurable nonnegative summands justify exchanging sum and integral without σ-finiteness. Translation isometry identifies each restricted plane measure, and Measure.sum_apply plus extensionality proves the exact identity. Neither dim V = n nor Z ⊆ Vᗮ is needed.

subproblem.title: Ball estimate for a product measure: ν(B_r(x)) ≤ ω_nrⁿσ(B_r(x − p_V x))
subproblem.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ. Let V ⊆ ℝ^P be a linear subspace with dim V = n (Module.finrank ℝ V = n), and p_V the orthogonal projection of ℝ^P onto V (V.starProjection). Let σ be a Borel measure on ℝ^P with σ(ℝ^P∖V^⊥) = 0, and ν a Borel measure on ℝ^P with ν(A) = ∫⁻_{t∈V}σ({y : t + y ∈ A}) dHⁿ(t) for every Borel A ⊆ ℝ^P (Hⁿ = μHE[n], lower Lebesgue integral over V). Then for every x ∈ ℝ^P and every r > 0, ν(B_r(x)) ≤ ω_n·ofReal(rⁿ)·σ(B_r(x − p_V x)), where ω_n = unitBallVolume n and B_r denotes an open ball.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (ν σ : Measure (Euclid P)) (V : Submodule ℝ (Euclid P)), Module.finrank ℝ V = n → σ (Vᗮ : Set (Euclid P))ᶜ = 0 → (∀ A : Set (Euclid P), MeasurableSet A → ν A = ∫⁻ t in (V : Set (Euclid P)), σ ((fun y => t + y) ⁻¹' A) ∂μHE[n]) → ∀ (x : Euclid P) (r : ℝ), 0 < r → ν (ball x r) ≤ unitBallVolume n * ENNReal.ofReal (r ^ n) * σ (ball (x - V.starProjection x) r)
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: step 1 ("Upper bound") of the parent proof, with q x written as x − p_V x (the orthogonal projection of x onto V^⊥). Uses the sibling subspace_ball (accepted idtp_tdc_subspace_ball_measure): Hⁿ(Q ∩ B_ρ(u)) = ω_n·ofReal(ρⁿ) for a subspace Q with dim Q = n, u ∈ Q and ρ > 0.
Notation: (D) is the hypothesis ν(A) = ∫⁻_{t∈V}σ({y : t + y ∈ A}) dHⁿ(t) for Borel A. Fix x ∈ ℝ^P and r > 0, and put p₀ := p_V x and q₀ := x − p_V x. Then p₀ ∈ V (Mathlib Submodule.starProjection_apply_mem), q₀ ∈ V^⊥ (Submodule.sub_starProjection_mem_orthogonal) and x = p₀ + q₀.
1. (Pythagoras.) Let t ∈ V and z ∈ V^⊥ with t + z ∈ B_r(x). Then (t + z) − x = (t − p₀) + (z − q₀). Here t − p₀ ∈ V and z − q₀ ∈ V^⊥, because subspaces are closed under subtraction. Hence ⟨t − p₀, z − q₀⟩ = 0 (Submodule.inner_right_of_mem_orthogonal), and Pythagoras (norm_add_sq_eq_norm_sq_add_norm_sq_real) gives ‖t + z − x‖² = ‖t − p₀‖² + ‖z − q₀‖². Since ‖t + z − x‖ = dist(t + z, x) < r and all three norms are ≥ 0, we get ‖t − p₀‖² ≤ ‖t + z − x‖² < r² and ‖z − q₀‖² ≤ ‖t + z − x‖² < r². As r > 0, ‖t − p₀‖ < r and ‖z − q₀‖ < r, i.e. t ∈ B_r(p₀) and z ∈ B_r(q₀).
2. (Pointwise bound.) For t ∈ V let S_t := {y : t + y ∈ B_r(x)}. Since σ(ℝ^P∖V^⊥) = 0, σ(S_t) = σ(S_t ∩ V^⊥) (measure_inter_conull). If t ∈ B_r(p₀), every z ∈ S_t ∩ V^⊥ satisfies t + z ∈ B_r(x), so z ∈ B_r(q₀) by step 1; thus S_t ∩ V^⊥ ⊆ B_r(q₀) and σ(S_t) ≤ σ(B_r(q₀)). If t ∉ B_r(p₀), a point z ∈ S_t ∩ V^⊥ would force t ∈ B_r(p₀) by step 1, so S_t ∩ V^⊥ = ∅ and σ(S_t) = 0. In both cases σ(S_t) ≤ 1_{B_r(p₀)}(t)·σ(B_r(q₀)) for every t ∈ V, where 1_{B_r(p₀)} is the {0, 1}-valued indicator function.
3. (Integration.) B_r(x) is open, hence Borel, so (D) gives ν(B_r(x)) = ∫⁻_{t∈V}σ(S_t) dHⁿ(t). V is a finite-dimensional, hence closed, hence Borel subset of ℝ^P. So step 2 and monotonicity of the set lower integral (setLIntegral_mono') give ν(B_r(x)) ≤ ∫⁻_{t∈V}1_{B_r(p₀)}(t)·σ(B_r(q₀)) dHⁿ(t). Since B_r(p₀) is Borel, this integral equals σ(B_r(q₀))·(Hⁿ⌞V)(B_r(p₀)) = σ(B_r(q₀))·Hⁿ(V ∩ B_r(p₀)) (lintegral_indicator_const, Measure.restrict_apply).
4. (Disc measure.) Since dim V = n, p₀ ∈ V and r > 0, subspace_ball (with Q = V, y = p₀, ρ = r) gives Hⁿ(V ∩ B_r(p₀)) = ω_n·ofReal(rⁿ). Therefore ν(B_r(x)) ≤ σ(B_r(q₀))·ω_n·ofReal(rⁿ) = ω_n·ofReal(rⁿ)·σ(B_r(x − p_V x)) by commutativity of multiplication in [0, ∞]. ∎
proof_key_steps: Write x = p₀ + q₀ with p₀ = p_Vx ∈ V and q₀ = x − p_Vx ∈ V^⊥. For t ∈ V and z ∈ V^⊥, Pythagoras gives ‖t + z − x‖² = ‖t − p₀‖² + ‖z − q₀‖², so t + z ∈ B_r(x) forces t ∈ B_r(p₀) and z ∈ B_r(q₀).
Since σ is carried by V^⊥, σ({y : t + y ∈ B_r(x)}) ≤ 1_{B_r(p₀)}(t)·σ(B_r(q₀)) for every t ∈ V.
Integrating over V with the product formula gives ν(B_r(x)) ≤ σ(B_r(q₀))·Hⁿ(V ∩ B_r(p₀)).
subspace_ball gives Hⁿ(V ∩ B_r(p₀)) = ω_n·ofReal(rⁿ), which is the claimed bound.

audit.reason: All hypotheses match. Pythagoras gives both required ball inclusions; concentration on Vᗮ gives the indicator bound. Monotonicity of the lower integral and the declared subspace_ball dependency then prove the exact inequality. No unstated measurability or local-finiteness assumption is needed.

subproblem.title: A ν-a.e. transversal constraint holds σ-a.e.: if x − p_V x ∈ Z for ν-a.e. x, then σ(ℝ^P∖Z) = 0
subproblem.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ. Let V ⊆ ℝ^P be a linear subspace with dim V = n (Module.finrank ℝ V = n), and p_V the orthogonal projection of ℝ^P onto V (V.starProjection). Let σ be a Borel measure on ℝ^P with σ(ℝ^P∖V^⊥) = 0, and ν a Borel measure on ℝ^P with ν(A) = ∫⁻_{t∈V}σ({y : t + y ∈ A}) dHⁿ(t) for every Borel A ⊆ ℝ^P (Hⁿ = μHE[n]). Let Z ⊆ ℝ^P be a Borel set such that x − p_V x ∈ Z for ν-almost every x. Then σ(ℝ^P∖Z) = 0.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (ν σ : Measure (Euclid P)) (V : Submodule ℝ (Euclid P)) (Z : Set (Euclid P)), Module.finrank ℝ V = n → σ (Vᗮ : Set (Euclid P))ᶜ = 0 → (∀ A : Set (Euclid P), MeasurableSet A → ν A = ∫⁻ t in (V : Set (Euclid P)), σ ((fun y => t + y) ⁻¹' A) ∂μHE[n]) → MeasurableSet Z → (∀ᵐ x ∂ν, x - V.starProjection x ∈ Z) → σ Zᶜ = 0
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: step 4 ("σ lives on Z") of the parent proof, for an arbitrary Borel set Z. In the parent, Z = {w ∈ V^⊥ : ofReal c ≤ σ({w})}, which is countable and hence Borel, and q x = x − p_V x. Uses the sibling subspace_ball (accepted idtp_tdc_subspace_ball_measure).
Notation: (D) is the hypothesis ν(A) = ∫⁻_{t∈V}σ({y : t + y ∈ A}) dHⁿ(t) for Borel A, and q(y) := y − p_V y. The map q is continuous because p_V is a continuous linear map.
1. (The set E.) Let E := q⁻¹(ℝ^P∖Z) = {y : y − p_V y ∉ Z}. As Z is Borel and q is continuous (hence Borel measurable), E is Borel.
2. (ν(E) = 0.) The hypothesis states that q(x) ∈ Z for ν-a.e. x, i.e. ν({x : q(x) ∉ Z}) = 0 (ae_iff), and this set is E.
3. (Invariance under V.) Let t ∈ V and y ∈ ℝ^P. By linearity p_V(t + y) = p_V t + p_V y, and p_V t = t because t ∈ V (Submodule.starProjection_eq_self_iff). Hence q(t + y) = (t + y) − (t + p_V y) = y − p_V y = q(y), so t + y ∈ E ⟺ y ∈ E. That is, {y : t + y ∈ E} = E for every t ∈ V.
4. (Product formula.) V is finite-dimensional, hence closed, hence Borel. Apply (D) to A = E (Borel by step 1) and use step 3: ν(E) = ∫⁻_{t∈V}σ({y : t + y ∈ E}) dHⁿ(t) = ∫⁻_{t∈V}σ(E) dHⁿ(t), since the integrands agree at every t ∈ V (setLIntegral_congr_fun). The last integral equals σ(E)·Hⁿ(V) (setLIntegral_const).
5. (Hⁿ(V) > 0.) Since 0 ∈ V, dim V = n and 1 > 0, subspace_ball (Q = V, y = 0, ρ = 1) gives Hⁿ(V ∩ B_1(0)) = ω_n·ofReal(1ⁿ) = ω_n. Here ω_n = unitBallVolume n is the Lebesgue measure of the open unit ball of ℝⁿ = Euclid n. It is positive because Lebesgue measure on Euclid n is an additive Haar measure, positive on nonempty open sets (measure_ball_pos). This includes n = 0, where Euclid 0 is a single point of measure 1. As V ∩ B_1(0) ⊆ V, Hⁿ(V) ≥ ω_n > 0.
6. (σ(E) = 0.) By steps 2 and 4, σ(E)·Hⁿ(V) = 0. A product in [0, ∞] is 0 only if a factor is 0 (mul_eq_zero), and Hⁿ(V) ≠ 0 by step 5, so σ(E) = 0.
7. (Conclusion.) We show ℝ^P∖Z ⊆ E ∪ (ℝ^P∖V^⊥). Let w ∉ Z. If w ∈ V^⊥, then p_V w = 0 (Submodule.starProjection_apply_eq_zero_iff), so q(w) = w ∉ Z and w ∈ E. Otherwise w ∈ ℝ^P∖V^⊥. By monotonicity and subadditivity of σ, σ(ℝ^P∖Z) ≤ σ(E) + σ(ℝ^P∖V^⊥) = 0 + 0 = 0, using step 6 and the hypothesis σ(ℝ^P∖V^⊥) = 0 (measure_union_null, measure_mono_null). ∎
proof_key_steps: E := {y : y − p_Vy ∉ Z} is Borel, and ν(E) = 0 by the a.e. hypothesis.
p_V(t + y) = t + p_Vy for t ∈ V, so E is invariant under translations by V, and the product formula gives ν(E) = σ(E)·Hⁿ(V).
Hⁿ(V) ≥ Hⁿ(V ∩ B_1(0)) = ω_n > 0 (subspace_ball, measure_ball_pos), hence σ(E) = 0.
ℝ^P∖Z ⊆ E ∪ (ℝ^P∖V^⊥) because p_Vw = 0 for w ∈ V^⊥, so σ(ℝ^P∖Z) = 0.

audit.reason: The proof establishes that E is Borel, ν-null and invariant under V-translations. The product formula gives σ(E)·Hⁿ(V) = 0; subspace_ball supplies Hⁿ(V) > 0, including n = 0. Concentration on Vᗮ then gives σ(Zᶜ) = 0. All assumptions and dependencies are explicit.
